# A functional component destroyed mid-update freezes its ancestors' updates

## Context

Found while attributing a unit flake on neo #19825 (run 38948640859, job 117135130702, at `07b3c818d1`). `ViewLoadingReprojection.spec.mjs` › "the expected teardown cancellation is consumed silently" records every `console.error` for 50 ms and expects none. It caught `vdom update wedged: "cmp-scroll-1"`. That id belongs to the functional `MockComponent` of `unit/functional/ScrollState.spec.mjs`, which that spec destroys in its `afterEach`. A destroyed component's wedge watchdog fired into another spec's window. The same PR had an earlier red in this spec at `:159`.

A local unit probe on `dev` `eedc33c3dd` registers a flight that never replies, then destroys the component:

| component destroyed mid-flight | after `destroy()` | 120 ms later (threshold 50 ms) | its parent's next update, 400 ms later |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component.Base` (control) | in-flight entry and watchdog released; gone from the parent's `descendantInFlightMap` | no error | resolved |
| `functional.component.Base` | in-flight entry and watchdog still set; still in the parent's map | `vdom update wedged: "neo-functional-component-1"` | **still pending** |

## The Problem

Destroying a functional component during its VDOM flight leaves the flight registered. The dead component then:
- gets reported as wedged by the watchdog, a false alarm and a cross-spec flake source;
- stays in each ancestor's `descendantInFlightMap`, so an ancestor's next update yields to it and never settles. In an app, the parent container stops updating.

## The Architectural Reality

- `VdomLifecycle` registers flights through `VDomUpdate.registerInFlightUpdate`. `component.Abstract` mixes it in for both component families: `component.Base` and `functional.component.Base` both extend `Abstract`.
- #14923 (#14911) made destruction "a complete render-flight cancellation boundary" with three calls: `rejectCallbacks(id, Neo.isDestroyed)`, `unregisterInFlightUpdate(id)` and `triggerPostUpdates(id)`. It placed them in `component.Base#destroy` (`src/component/Base.mjs:1415–1426`), so the functional family never got them. `Abstract#destroy` (`src/component/Abstract.mjs:361–366`) has none.
- `unregisterInFlightUpdate` is also what clears the watchdog timer and removes the id from every parent's `descendantInFlightMap` (`src/manager/VDomUpdate.mjs:702–720`).
- Design authority: #14911 / #14923, and `component.Base#destroy`'s own comment ("a lingering one makes every ancestor update yield to it forever").

## The Fix

- Move the boundary, its three calls and their comment, from `component.Base#destroy` to the top of `component.Abstract#destroy`, the class that mixes in `VdomLifecycle`.
- `component.Base` keeps its order: its own teardown, then `super.destroy()`, which now runs the boundary before `Abstract`'s DOM-event and registry teardown, as before.
- `functional.component.Base#destroy` reaches it through `super.destroy()`.
- Lines move; no line is added beyond the move.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: a functional component destroyed during a flight releases its in-flight entry and watchdog, and no "wedged" error follows. Unit test in `VdomDestroyCancellation.spec.mjs`, red on `dev`.
- [x] AC-2: its parent's next update resolves. Unit test, red on `dev`: pending.
- [x] AC-3: `component.Base`'s existing cancellation arms stay green and unchanged, and the promises parked on a functional flight settle with the destroy sentinel.
- [x] AC-4: the full unit suite and the component suites pass.

## Out of Scope

- `ViewLoadingReprojection.spec.mjs`'s capture window, which accepts any `console.error` in the worker. With this fix the dead component no longer writes there, but the window stays broad; a separate hygiene question.
- Why `ScrollState.spec.mjs` leaves a flight open at teardown: a test needs to be able to destroy a component mid-flight.
